findings: The primary specimen convincingly depicts Great Crested Flycatcher: a large, lean, broad-shouldered flycatcher with a large subtly crested head, thick straight bill, brownish-gray head and breast, lemon-yellow belly, rufous wing panels, and a long rufous-brown tail.

The specimen has one head, one bill, one visible eye, one tail, and anatomically coherent wings, legs, and gripping feet; far-side structures are naturally occluded. The detached wing and bill/head studies are clearly supplementary and independently well formed.

The main and supplementary bills have coherent upper and lower mandibles from base to tip, with a correctly shown pale lower-mandible base and no truncated, reversed, or materially inconsistent projection.

Every visible title, taxonomy line, measurement, habitat statement, behavior statement, field-mark line, study label, and palette label is legible and matches the proposed profile without duplicated, omitted, substituted, or nonsensical wording.

The body-length diagram correctly places 17 cm (6.7 in) at the bottom and 22 cm (8.7 in) at the top. Values increase upward, units agree, no marker contradicts the endpoints, and “SCHEMATIC — NOT TO SCALE” clearly prevents interpretation as the printed specimen’s scale.

The proposed measurements are supportable across the allowed direct sources: Audubon publishes 20–22 cm length, 33–38 cm wingspan, and 27–40 g weight; All About Birds publishes 17–21 cm, 34 cm, and 27–40 g. Their differing measurement conventions do not establish a two-domain conflict with the synthesized profile range.
All specified composition elements now remain at least 60 pixels from the portrait edges, including the title, right-side ruler, supplementary studies, palette swatches, and bottom labels.
No place name, ZIP code, coordinates, map, or local-observation detail appears.
